newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ABARE lowers forecast Australian sugar crop.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ABARE lowers forecast Australian sugar crop.

text.p: Australia's official commodities forecaster, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE), has lowered its forecast of Australian sugar production to 5.3 million tonnes in 1996/97 (September to August) from its previous forecast of 5.5 million tonnes.

Production at the latest forecast level would be up 6.9 percent on 1995/96, stemming mainly from a five percent increase in area harvested, ABARE said. Sugar from the Ord river region in northern Western Australia would contribute to the higher output, with the first substantial sugar cane crop expected to reach about 40,000 tonnes in 1996/97.
"The sugar content of cane is expected to be similar to that of Queensland farms but yields of cane per hectare are expected to be around 80 percent higher," ABARE said.
Exports were forecast to rise 4.1 percent to 4.1 million tonnes, but the value of exports was forecast to fall 12.3 percent to about A$1.4 billion, reflecting lower world prices.
Returns to Australian sugar producers were forecast to fall 8.5 percent in 1996/97 to average A$333/tonne.
ABARE said world sugar prices were forecast to fall by 14 percent to 10.8 cents/lb in 1996/97.
"Production of sugar is forecast to exceed consumption by around four million tonnes, leading to an increase in world stocks and lower prices in 1996/97," it said.
However, world production was forecast to fall slightly from the record 126 million tonnes produced in 1995/96. The decline would stem mainly from lower production in India and Ukraine.
